original_question: Does there exist a Steiner system S(4, 5, 21), that is, a 21-element set together with a collection of 5-element blocks such that every 4-element subset is contained in exactly one block? Equivalently, is the sequence (1, 21, 210, 1330, 5985, 1197) a pure O-sequence?
target_in_paper: Section 3’s unlabeled open existence statement about Steiner quintuple systems: the paper says that the smallest value of r for which the existence of S(4,5,r) is open is r=21, and 'in other words' it is unknown whether (1,21,210,1330,5985,1197) is a pure O-sequence.
correct_elements: Your draft already identifies the exact open case discussed in the paper: the Steiner quintuple system S(4,5,21). It also correctly gives the associated sequence (1,21,210,1330,5985,1197) and matches the paper’s pure-O-sequence reformulation. So the mathematical target is essentially right.
missing_details: The paper frames this as an open existence statement in the Steiner-system discussion of Section 3, not as a named conjecture or a broader classification problem.

To make the pure-O-sequence side stand alone, one should define a pure O-sequence as the h-vector of a finite monomial order ideal closed under divisibility whose maximal monomials all have the same degree.
The ambient polynomial ring should be specified as K[y1,...,y21]; the paper notes that whether a sequence is a pure O-sequence does not depend on the field K.
The degree data should be attached to the order ideal explicitly: 1 monomial of degree 0, 21 of degree 1, 210 of degree 2, 1330 of degree 3, 5985 of degree 4, and 1197 maximal monomials of degree 5.

In the Steiner-system formulation, the relevant generators are squarefree degree-5 monomials/5-subsets, so the intermediary object is really a pure f-vector (a squarefree pure O-sequence), even though the paper states the final reformulation directly as a pure O-sequence.
If one wants the equivalence to be fully explicit, one should say that the 1197 blocks correspond to the 1197 maximal degree-5 generators and that every 4-subset occurs in exactly one block.
refined_question: Does there exist, over some (equivalently any) field K, a pure monomial order ideal X in K[y1,...,y21] whose maximal monomials all have degree 5 and whose degree counts are h(X)=(1,21,210,1330,5985,1197)? In other words, is (1,21,210,1330,5985,1197) a pure O-sequence?
equivalent_formulation: Does there exist a Steiner quintuple system S(4,5,21), i.e. a collection of 1197 five-element subsets of a 21-element set such that every four-element subset is contained in exactly one block?
justification: The draft clearly targets the Steiner-design discussion in Section 3, not the matroid material or the later list of open problems. After defining Steiner systems and explaining that their existence corresponds to appropriate pure f-vectors/pure O-sequences (Section 3, unlabeled Steiner-system discussion, p. 9; Example 3.2, pp. 9-10), the paper states specifically that 'the smallest value of r for which the existence of S(4,5,r) is currently open is 21' and, 'in other words,' that it is unknown whether (1,21,210,1330,5985,1197) is a pure O-sequence (Section 3, unlabeled open statement on Steiner quintuple systems, p. 11). To make the question fully stand-alone, one must import the paper’s definition of a pure O-sequence and its field-independence from Section 2 (beginning of Section 2, p. 1).
